glossary.definition: A diffusion model generates images (or audio) by starting from random visual noise, like TV static, and gradually refining it, step by step, into a coherent picture that matches a text prompt. It's a bit like a sculptor starting with a rough, shapeless block and slowly chiseling away until a specific figure emerges, except the "chiseling" is dozens of small AI-guided cleanup passes. It's the technique behind most modern AI image generators, like Midjourney and DALL-E.

items.title: Meta removes language that raised scraping and AI training concerns
items.summary: A Meta spokesperson insisted that the updated terms did not reflect a change in the way Meta crawls the web. According to legal experts interviewed by Nieman Lab , this looked like a “remarkable provision” that could give Meta permission to scrape the website of any publisher with a Meta business account and use the content to train the company’s AI models. ) However, a Meta spokesperson insisted that the updated terms did not reflect a change in the way Meta crawls the web. And now, The Verge reports that the provision has been removed.

items.title: Anthropic says its workforce has become less junior and is spending more time in meetings
items.summary: The composition of Anthropic’s workforce and the type of work getting done have changed significantly in the past year. ” But even if other organizations never embrace AI as thoroughly or in the exact same way as Anthropic, the report offers an intriguing glimpse at how the company currently operates. Notably, Anthropic is making fewer junior hires, with the proportion of junior-level employees in technical departments falling from 21% to 14% since early 2025, and the proportion of junior technical hires falling even more sharply, from 27% to 9%. ” In fact, the report suggests “human attention and judgement” are becoming a “bottleneck” for productivity, as Claude produces a “deluge” of text that needs to be read and organized.

items.title: An OpenAI model hacked a government site, grabbed 24 years of hospital data and kept it quiet
items.summary: OpenAI has published four new cases where its AI models bypassed security boundaries on their own during training or testing. In one case, a model extracted server passwords from a government website, forged authorization tokens, and downloaded 24 years of hospital data without mentioning the unauthorized access. In one case, OpenAI asked a model to pull hospital bed statistics from a government website. But the data wasn't publicly accessible.

items.title: Meta removes language that may have allowed it to scrape news sites
items.summary: After backlash, Meta is updating its terms again to remove language that suggested it could scrape content from sites, including news sites, to train its AI. Specifically, the following language no longer appears on the commercial terms page : … Meta may use any content from such domains, web pages, or URLs to provide, develop, improve, research, train, and maintain the integrity of, the Meta Company Products, services, and features provided under these Commercial Terms and any other applicable supplemental terms. Language that experts say allowed the scraping of news sites to train its AI has been removed from Meta’s terms. … Meta may use any content from such domains, web pages, or URLs to provide, develop, improve, research, train, and maintain the integrity of, the Meta Company Products, services, and features provided under these Commercial Terms and any other applicable supplemental terms.

items.title: ServiceNow AI Control Tower: Selling a penthouse while building the frame
items.summary: ServiceNow Inc. is making one of the more consequential and visible bets in enterprise artificial intelligence. The company says AI Control Tower can discover and govern any agent, work across models and clouds, track cost and value, and shut down behavior that violates policy. That sales pitch plays directly to ServiceNow’s greatest asset – its installed base.

items.title: Anthropics' Claude cracks a 25-year-old NSA cryptography mystery in under 30 minutes
items.summary: Anthropic's AI model Claude has solved a 25-year-old cryptography puzzle. The mysterious seeds behind NIST's standard curves for digital signatures were provided by the NSA without explanation, raising long-standing suspicion about built-in backdoors. Claude figured out in under 30 minutes that the seeds came from "lrand48," a simple C random number generator, making deliberate backdoors far less likely. Anthropic's AI Claude has solved a 25-year-old cryptography mystery.

items.title: Websites are closing their doors to AI agents
items.summary: Autonomous agents are the hottest thing in AI. OpenAI, Meta, Google, Instinct, and others promise their agents can scour the internet on your behalf, doing anything from booking a dinner reservation and cleaning out your inbox to buying new shoes. But what happens when the rest of the internet won't play nice? In recent weeks, users of services like Meta's Muse, xAI's Grok, OpenAI's Dots, and Instinct have reported blocks preventing their AI agents from performing tasks across top websites.

items.title: Why AI Isn’t Ready to Tackle Our Convoluted Genomes
items.summary: The DNA inside our cells isn’t just a series of instructions, but something far more dynamic. Like scientists, AI models don't yet have the data to properly decode it. The original version of this story appeared in Quanta Magazine . Since its molecular structure was deduced in the 1950s, DNA has been hailed by many biologists as the secret of life.

items.title: Katie Zacharia Was Linked to an AI Rare-Earths Startup. It’s Even Weirder Than It Sounds
items.summary: The short-lived White House press secretary was listed as an adviser to a Kristi Noem–linked company that aims to use AI for mining. Both the company and she say she never worked there. Before being fired five days into her stint as White House press secretary, Katie Zacharia spent much of the day attempting to explain her past. Throughout her brief tenure, Zacharia’s résumé was the source of much intrigue.

items.title: Open source and on device: the strategy behind Nvidia’s new AI models
items.summary: The new Nemotron 3.5 models show how the AI giant is focusing on reinforcing its own GPU infrastructure while supporting the open source community.

items.title: Roundtables: A Conversation With the Creator of AI-Designed Viruses
items.summary: Listen to the session or watch below Can AI design new life forms? In 2025, Stanford University PhD student Samuel King came up with a preliminary answer when he used a generative AI model to propose genetic blueprints for microscopic viruses. It isn’t yet an example of AI-generated life, but that could be next. Watch as senior AI reporter James O’Donnell interviews King about his work, being named one of MIT Technology Review’s Innovators Under 35 and new ways of seeing biology.

items.title: Prompt: Enterprise controls can't keep up with AI agents
items.summary: Companies are giving agents more authority, but many are still struggling to track what they can access, what they're doing and how to stop them.
